sentences.en: In the summer of 19 BC, the poet Publius Vergilius Maro, better known as Virgil, was travelling in Greece when he caught a fever.
sentences.zh: 公元前19年夏天，诗人普布利乌斯·韦吉利乌斯·马罗（人们更熟悉他的名字维吉尔）在希腊旅行时染上了高烧。
zh_words: 普布利乌斯·韦吉利乌斯·马罗

sentences.en: He took ship back to Italy, but died when he reached the port of Brindisi.
sentences.zh: 他乘船返回意大利，但在抵达布林迪西港时去世了。

sentences.en: He was just 50 years old.
sentences.zh: 他当时年仅50岁。

sentences.en: But that was not the end of Publius Vergilius Maro.
sentences.zh: 但这并非普布利乌斯·韦吉利乌斯·马罗的终点。
zh_words: 普布利乌斯·韦吉利乌斯·马罗

sentences.en: More than a thousand years later, on the night before Good Friday 1300, another Italian poet found himself lost in a dark wood.
sentences.zh: 一千多年后，在1300年耶稣受难日前夕的夜晚，另一位意大利诗人发现自己迷失在了一片黑暗的森林中。

sentences.en: And who should appear to guide him through the underworld but the ghost?
sentences.zh: 还有谁会现身引导他穿过阴间呢，除了那个鬼魂？

sentences.en: Of Virgil.
sentences.zh: 也就是维吉尔的鬼魂。

sentences.en: So begins Dante Alighieri's The Divine Comedy, one of the absolute foundational texts of European and world literature.
sentences.zh: 但丁·阿利吉耶里的《神曲》就这样拉开了序幕，这是欧洲乃至世界文学绝对的基石文本之一。

sentences.en: And Tom Holland, that's a really good example, isn't it, of the imprint that the classical world, Greece and Rome, has left on our imagination.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·霍兰，这真的是个极好的例子，不是吗？体现了古典世界——希腊和罗马——对我们想象力留下的烙印。

sentences.en: Do you think we're all kind of the children of Greece and Rome, really?
sentences.zh: 你觉得我们其实都是希腊和罗马的后代吗？

sentences.en: Well, you know I have views on that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道我对这个是有看法的。

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 我是这么认为的。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: We look back to Greece and Rome as a kind of seedbed of ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们将希腊和罗马视为我们自身的某种发源地。

sentences.en: There are other influences on us as well that perhaps we might come on to.
sentences.zh: 我们身上也受到其他文化的影响，也许我们后面会谈到。

sentences.en: They're the ones we talk about, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 但这些正是我们常谈论的，不是吗？

sentences.en: They're the ones we talk about moSt.
sentences.zh: 这些正是我们谈论得最多的。

sentences.en: The history of how people have understood Greece and Rome since the kind of the end of the classical age is itself a massive theme of history.
sentences.zh: 自古典时代结束以来，人们如何理解希腊和罗马的历史，本身就是历史上的一个宏大主题。

sentences.en: So, I mean, you cited Dante.
sentences.zh: 所以，我是说，你提到了但丁。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a kind of classic example.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个经典的例子。

sentences.en: Dante's the great classic of Italian literature.
sentences.zh: 但丁是意大利文学伟大的经典。

sentences.en: And Virgil has this absolutely starring role in it.
sentences.zh: 而维吉尔在其中扮演了绝对的主角。

sentences.en: And I remember something that probably the most famous classicist in the world,
sentences.zh: 我记得可能当今世界上最著名的古典学者，

sentences.en: Mary Beard, said once, ages ago.
sentences.zh: 玛丽·比尔德，很久以前说过的一句话。

sentences.en: I think it was long before she'd kind of become a global superstar.
sentences.zh: 我想那是她成为全球超级巨星很久之前的事了。

sentences.en: And she gave a lecture and she talked about Virgil.
sentences.zh: 她当时做了一场讲座，谈到了维吉尔。

sentences.en: And she said that it was her opinion that pretty much since the moment Virgil had laid down his pen to die, there wasn't a day when someone hadn't read the Aeneid.
sentences.zh: 她说，据她所见，几乎自从维吉尔放下笔离世的那一刻起，就没有哪一天是没人读过《埃涅阿斯纪》的。

sentences.en: It's amazing.
sentences.zh: 这太惊人了。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And so if we're going to talk about this, this kind of this legacy, the way that the legacy of Greece and Rome has kind of evolved and spread over the course of the centuries
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们打算讨论这个，这种遗产，希腊和罗马的遗产在漫长世纪和千禧年间演变和传播的方式，

sentences.en: and the millennia, who better to have on the show than the Imperatrix, the Basilea herself,
sentences.zh: 还有谁比“女统治者”、比“女皇”本人更适合来到节目中呢？

sentences.en: Mary Beard.
sentences.zh: 也就是玛丽·比尔德。

sentences.en: So, Mary, thank you so much for agreeing to come on and talk to us about this subject, which is a subject that is actually very much on you, has been on your mind recently,
sentences.zh: 玛丽，非常感谢你应邀前来和我们谈论这个主题，实际上这也是你最近一直挂在心上的主题，

sentences.en: hasn't it?
sentences.zh: 不是吗？

sentences.en: Because you've just published a fantastic new book, The Twelve Caesars, which is about,
sentences.zh: 因为你刚刚出版了一本精彩的新书《十二凯撒》，这本书讲的是，

sentences.en: it's not actually about the Twelve Caesars themselves, but about how they've been understood.
sentences.zh: 其实不是关于十二凯撒本身，而是关于人们是如何理解他们的。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: And the book is saying, look, you know, every time we go to a stately home, you know, what do we see?
sentences.zh: 书里提到，看吧，每次我们去那种豪华宅邸，你知道，我们看到了什么？

sentences.en: We see a lineup of Twelve Caesars, probably a rather vulgar porphyry or something, with a bit of gilding.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了一排十二凯撒的雕像，可能带着点俗气的斑岩材质或者别的什么，还带点镀金。

sentences.en: And now even people like me tend to walk past, you know, and think, yeah, Twelve Caesars, on we go.
sentences.zh: 现在就连像我这样的人，走过时往往也会想，好吧，十二凯撒，走吧。

sentences.en: And what I've done in the book, and it fits very much with, you know, the whole idea of why the ancient world still matters to us.
sentences.zh: 我在书中做的事，非常契合古代世界对我们而言为何仍然重要的整个理念。

sentences.en: You know, I started to ask, why?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我开始追问：为什么？

sentences.en: What are these tyrants doing on our shelves?
sentences.zh: 为什么这些暴君会摆在我们的书架上？

sentences.en: You know, why are we still so interested in Caesars?
sentences.zh: 你知道，为什么我们对凯撒仍然如此感兴趣？

sentences.en: I mean, you're right to say, you know, I don't think Nero quite comes up to Virgil.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你说得对，尼禄大概没法跟维吉尔相比。

sentences.en: But in terms of the visual world in which we live, we're still surrounded by these guys.
sentences.zh: 但就我们赖以生存的视觉世界而言，我们依然被这些家伙环绕着。

sentences.en: We still use it.
sentences.zh: 我们还在使用这些形象。

sentences.en: Even people who say, oh, I know nothing about the ancient world, which people often say, and they're always wrong, because they always do.
sentences.zh: 甚至那些说“哦，我对古代世界一无所知”的人——人们经常这么说，而且他们总是错的，因为他们其实懂。

sentences.en: They're always wrong when they say that.
sentences.zh: 当他们这么说的时候，总是错的。

sentences.en: But, you know, it's often the starting convo with me, you know, oh, I know nothing about the ancient world.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，这经常是我开始对话的开场白，哦，我对古代世界一无所知。

sentences.en: People still pick up a newspaper.
sentences.zh: 人们依然会拿起一份报纸。

sentences.en: There's a cartoon of some politician who doesn't really have his mind on the job.
sentences.zh: 上面有一幅漫画，画着某个并不真正在乎工作的政客。

sentences.en: You know, he's dressed up with a toga and a laurel wreath.
sentences.zh: 你看，他穿着托加长袍，戴着月桂花环。

sentences.en: And he's strumming a lyre and this blazing fire in the background.
sentences.zh: 他正弹奏着里拉琴，背景是一片熊熊烈火。

sentences.en: And we all know it's Nero fiddling while Rome burned.
sentences.zh: 我们都知道那是“尼禄在罗马城燃烧时弹琴”。

sentences.en: We do, we do.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，我们当然知道。

sentences.en: And so, Mary, the critics have been raving about this book.
sentences.zh: 所以，玛丽，评论界对这本书赞不绝口。

sentences.en: I'm going to quote one particularly distinguished critic who has written, as this book triumphantly demonstrates, there is no one on the face of the planet
sentences.zh: 我要引用一位特别杰出的评论家的话，他写道：正如这本书所胜利展现的那样，地球上没有人

sentences.en: better qualified than Mary Beard to guide us through the great hall of mirrors, labyrinthine and treacherous as it is, that separates us from the 12 Caesars.
sentences.zh: 比玛丽·比尔德更有资格引导我们穿过那座虽错综复杂且充满背叛、但却将我们与十二凯撒隔开的巨大镜厅。

sentences.en: Do you know who that distinguished critic was, don't you?
sentences.zh: 你知道那位杰出的评论家是谁，对吧？

sentences.en: Was it you?
sentences.zh: 是你吗？

sentences.en: It was.
sentences.zh: 正是。

sentences.en: You're quoting yourself.
sentences.zh: 你在引用你自己。

sentences.en: I am.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I'm quoting myself.
sentences.zh: 我在引用我自己。

sentences.en: That's shame.
sentences.zh: 真丢脸。

sentences.en: Mary, this is Harold Lee's process.
sentences.zh: 玛丽，这就是哈罗德·李的流程。

sentences.en: I know this is your first time in this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我知道这是你第一次上这个播客。

sentences.en: This is how it proceeds.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这么进行的。

sentences.en: Tom compliments himself a great length.
sentences.zh: 汤姆大肆自我赞美了一番。

sentences.en: I'm not.
sentences.zh: 我没有。

sentences.en: I'm complimenting Mary.
sentences.zh: 我在赞美玛丽。

sentences.en: I'm complimenting Mary.
sentences.zh: 我在赞美玛丽。

sentences.en: But the reason I cite that is that I've actually rather, yeah, I am going to compliment myself here because I do like that idea of a great hall of mirrors, labyrinthine and
sentences.zh: 但我之所以引用那个，是因为我其实挺——对，我这里确实要赞美一下我自己，因为我真的很喜欢“巨大镜厅，错综复杂又充满背叛”这个比喻。

sentences.en: treacherous.
sentences.zh: 充满背叛。

sentences.en: Because Mary, that, I mean, go on, tell me.
sentences.zh: 因为玛丽，那个——来吧，告诉我。

sentences.en: I mean, that's okay.
sentences.zh: 我是说，没关系。

sentences.en: That's a good description.
sentences.zh: 那是个很好的描述。

sentences.en: Oh, it is.
sentences.zh: 哦，确实是。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You're a great wordsmith, Tom Holland, a great wordsmith.
sentences.zh: 你是个出色的词匠，汤姆·霍兰，真正的词匠。

sentences.en: Because the thing is that there is no one way to respond to it.
sentences.zh: 因为问题在于，人们并没有单一的方式去回应它。

sentences.en: And so obviously different ages have understood this in different ways.
sentences.zh: 因此，显而易见，不同的时代以不同的方式理解了这一点。

sentences.en: So the Roman Empire collapses in the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 所以罗马帝国在西方崩溃了。

sentences.en: And that's an important thing because obviously it continues in the EaSt.
sentences.zh: 这是一件重要的事情，因为显然它在东方延续下去了。

sentences.en: But in the West, the legacy of classical literature and the memory of Rome endures, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 但在西方，古典文学的遗产和对罗马的记忆依然长存，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think we now tend to think that, let's say, the rediscovery of classical antiquity,
sentences.zh: 我想我们现在往往会认为，比方说，对古典古代的重新发现，

sentences.en: you know, was part and parcel not only of an intellectual enterprise in the early Renaissance, but it was also part and parcel of very much elite culture, dynastic power.
sentences.zh: 不仅是早期文艺复兴时期知识探索的一部分，它也很大程度上是精英文化和王朝权力的一部分。

sentences.en: We think of, you know, the big guys, the warlords of the late Middle Ages, you know, seeing themselves as Roman emperors.
sentences.zh: 我们会想到，那些中世纪末期的大人物、军阀们，将自己视为罗马皇帝。

sentences.en: And I think all that's true, but what I think is truer, both about images of emperors, but also about images of classical world in general, is that,
sentences.zh: 我认为这些都是真的，但我认为更真实的是——无论是关于皇帝的形象，还是关于整个古典世界的形象——

sentences.en: and I suppose this is what you're talking about when you mention Hall of Mirrors, these figures have always been much more kind of fragile, ambivalent,
sentences.zh: 我想这就是你提到镜厅时所谈论的，这些人物一直以来都更加脆弱、矛盾、

sentences.en: difficult to pin down, curious.
sentences.zh: 难以捉摸、充满神秘色彩。

sentences.en: And one of the things that I'm wanting to do in the book, you know, is actually to say, look, everybody, what did people in, let's say, 15th, 16th century know, think they knew?
sentences.zh: 我在书中想做的事情之一，其实就是说，听着，大家，15、16世纪的人们知道些什么，他们自以为知道些什么？

sentences.en: They might have been wrong.
sentences.zh: 他们可能搞错了。

sentences.en: What did they think they knew about the 12 Caesars, right?
sentences.zh: 他们对十二凯撒到底了解多少？

sentences.en: The first 12 Roman emperors, the most famous ones from Julius Caesar to Domitian, 12 rulers later.
sentences.zh: 前十二位罗马皇帝，从尤利乌斯·凯撒到多米提安，横跨十二位统治者，也是最著名的那些。

sentences.en: Well, they knew that all but one of them was rumoured to have had a not natural end.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他们知道除了其中一位之外，其余所有人都据传没有得到自然的结局。

sentences.en: They read their Suetonius and other bits of classical literature, and they knew that they were corrupt autocrats, et cetera, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 他们读过苏埃托尼乌斯和其他古典文学片段，他们知道这些人是腐败的独裁者，等等等等。

sentences.en: And yet, they use them, they use the image of these rulers, which they pick up from ancient sculpture, but particularly ancient coins.
sentences.zh: 然而，他们使用他们，利用从古代雕塑、尤其是古代硬币中提取的这些统治者形象。

sentences.en: And they decorate their private and public space with them.
sentences.zh: 他们用这些来装饰他们的私人和公共空间。

sentences.en: Now, we've sort of taken that for granted, you know, image of power, 12 Caesars.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们有点把这视为理所当然了，权力的象征，十二凯撒。

sentences.en: But actually, these figures are much more complicated than that.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，这些人物远比这要复杂得多。

sentences.en: And one of the questions I wanted to ask, and it become more relevant as my work on the book has gone on,
sentences.zh: 我想问的问题之一——随着我对这本书的研究深入，这个问题变得越来越重要——

sentences.en: is why did people want to see images of people they knew to be monsters in their homes, in their public spaces?
sentences.zh: 为什么人们会想在自己的家中、在公共空间里看到那些他们明知是怪物的形象？

sentences.en: And that leads you on to think, I think, a bit harder about, so what are these images for?
sentences.zh: 这会引导你去更深入地思考：那么这些图像究竟有什么用？

sentences.en: Or, you know, what are portraits of people from the past?
sentences.zh: 或者说，过去的肖像到底是什么？

sentences.en: You know, what are they doing?
sentences.zh: 它们在起什么作用？

sentences.en: What are they for?
sentences.zh: 它们是用来做什么的？

sentences.en: How do they fit into, whether it's the 19th century, the 15th century, or the 21st?
sentences.zh: 它们是如何融入无论是19世纪、15世纪还是21世纪的生活中的？

sentences.en: Mary, let me ask you a slightly different but kind of broader question.
sentences.zh: 玛丽，让我问你一个略有不同但更广泛的问题。

sentences.en: At what point do you think those people are aware of Greece and Rome as belonging to a different age,
sentences.zh: 你认为人们是在哪个时间点，开始意识到希腊和罗马属于一个不同的时代、

sentences.en: a vanished age, and not part of a continuum, not part of their own world, if you know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 一个消逝的时代，而不是连续统一体的一部分，也不是他们自己世界的一部分？如果你明白我的意思的话。

sentences.en: I think it's very hard to know.
sentences.zh: 我想这很难确切知道。

sentences.en: I mean, the standard answer would be, I suppose, you know, Renaissance, humanism, you know, burgeoning in the 15th century, and a little before and later.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，标准的答案大概是，文艺复兴时期的“人文主义”，在15世纪及其前后蓬勃发展。

sentences.en: In a sense, historicised the ancient world.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，它将古代世界历史化了。

sentences.en: It showed to the intellectuals of the West that the ancient world was a subject of study.
sentences.zh: 它向西方的知识分子表明，古代世界是一个研究对象。

sentences.en: It wasn't us.
sentences.zh: 它不再是我们。

sentences.en: And, you know, up to a point, that's true, you know, most of these...
sentences.zh: 而且，在某种程度上，这确实是真的，大多数这些……

sentences.en: Do you think it's important that, I mean, there's a difference here between pagan and Christian emperors, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 你认为这很重要吗？我的意思是，这里异教皇帝和基督教皇帝之间存在区别，不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, I think...
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为……

sentences.en: Or is there?
sentences.zh: 还是说其实没有？

sentences.en: That complicates things hugely, because, you know, I'm rather carefully in what I've just said to Dominic, sticking, you know, taking the intellectual line.
sentences.zh: 这把事情极大地复杂化了，因为，你知道，我在刚才对多米尼克所说的话里非常小心地坚持了知识分子的路线。

sentences.en: And suggesting, you know, hinting, which would be completely wrong, actually,
sentences.zh: 并且暗示着——这其实完全是错误的——

sentences.en: hinting that the engagement with these figures was, you know, was from people like me, only men in the Renaissance, you know.
sentences.zh: 暗示与这些人物的接触，仅仅来自像我这样的人，文艺复兴时期的男性，你知道的。

sentences.en: That there was a kind of humanistic academic inquiry, which, in a way, put a barrier.
sentences.zh: 存在一种人文主义的学术探究，它在某种程度上设置了一道屏障。

sentences.en: It both opened up the ancient world, but it made it seem different.
sentences.zh: 它既开启了古代世界，又让人觉得它与众不同。

sentences.en: And I think you'd also have to say there's a parallel strand going on, which I think a lot of us now,
sentences.zh: 我想你还得说，同时存在着另一条平行的脉络，我认为现在我们当中许多人并没有忘记，但在思考罗马皇帝时，它不会一下子涌入脑海，那就是基督教的历史其实已经嵌入其中。

sentences.en: we haven't forgotten, but doesn't come flooding in when you think about Roman emperors, which is that the history of Christianity is actually embedded.
sentences.zh: 基督教的历史嵌入在罗马帝国之中。

sentences.en: The history of Christianity is embedded in the Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 你知道，16世纪以来最受欢迎的一些绘画中，你也能在更早的时期找到一些例子。

sentences.en: You know, and, you know, some of the most popular paintings that you get from the 16th century onwards, but you can find some examples earlier.
sentences.zh: 这是一个我们现在几乎完全遗忘了的著名场景：奥古斯都皇帝在琢磨自己是否会变成神，

sentences.en: It's a famous scene that we've now almost uniformly forgotten of the Emperor Augustus wondering if he was going to become a god
sentences.zh: 并琢磨世上是否会有人比他更有权力。

sentences.en: and wondering if there was going to be anyone more powerful than him in the world.
sentences.zh: 于是他去咨询了一位异教女先知，即西比尔。

sentences.en: And he consults a pagan prophetess, a sybil.
sentences.zh: 她做了什么？

sentences.en: And what does she do?
sentences.zh: 她指向天空，而那正巧是耶稣诞生的那一天。

sentences.en: She points up in the sky and it's the very day that Jesus is being born.
sentences.zh: 奥古斯都在云端看到了玛丽和耶稣的幻象。

sentences.en: And Augustus has a vision of Mary and Jesus in a cloud.
sentences.zh: 他们的表现相当……你知道的，这些画家大多不擅长想象那个场景。

sentences.en: They do it rather, you know, they're not terribly good, most of these painters, at imagining that scene.
sentences.zh: 但我们要被告知的是，这两段历史交织在了一起。

sentences.en: But what we're being told is that those two histories come together.
sentences.zh: 在维吉尔身上也是如此，对吧？

sentences.en: And also in Virgil, right?
sentences.zh: 因为维吉尔之所以成为但丁的向导，原因之一就是人们曾相信他的诗作在某种程度上预言了基督的降临。

sentences.en: Because Virgil, I mean, one of the reasons why Virgil is Dante's guide is that it is believed that his poems, in a way, had foretold the coming of ChriSt.
sentences.zh: 因此，他变成了一种基督教式的死灵法师。

sentences.en: And therefore, he comes to become a kind of Christian necromancer.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 于是，耶稣诞生时，奥古斯都是执政的皇帝。

sentences.en: And so you get Augustus being the ruling emperor when Jesus was born.
sentences.zh: 而尼禄则成了大迫害者。

sentences.en: You get Nero as the great persecutor.
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果你去看圣彼得大教堂那些宏大的礼仪之门，那是古老而尊贵的圣彼得大教堂保留下来的新圣彼得大教堂的少数部分之一。

sentences.en: I mean, you go to the great ceremonial doors on St. Peter's, which are one of the few bits of new St. Peter's that were taken over from the venerable old St. Peter's.
sentences.zh: 你会在那里看到谁？

sentences.en: And who have you got?
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你以这种方式走进圣彼得大教堂时，你首先看到的是谁？

sentences.en: You know, who do you see first when you go into St. Peter's that way?
sentences.zh: 你看到了尼禄。

sentences.en: You see Nero.
sentences.zh: 这太惊人了。

sentences.en: That's amazing.
sentences.zh: 这太神奇了。

sentences.en: Nero is sitting there and he is condemning Peter and Paul to death.
sentences.zh: 尼禄就坐在那里，判处彼得和保罗死刑。

sentences.en: And so Roman emperors are absolutely built in to the idea of the history of the church from its very beginning to the time when the Roman Empire itself,
sentences.zh: 因此，罗马皇帝从教会历史的最初阶段一直到罗马帝国本身存在的时候，

sentences.en: at least from the point of view of the dynastic leaders, when Constantine would be the classic example, becomes himself a Christian when the Roman Empire becomes Christian.
sentences.zh: 至少从王朝统治者的角度来看——君士坦丁大帝就是一个典型的例子，当罗马帝国成为基督教国家时，他自己也成了一名基督徒。

sentences.en: So the whole of Christianity, I'm now going to say something completely outrageous and slightly wrong, but it's a good exaggeration.
sentences.zh: 因此，整个基督教史——我接下来要说的话可能听起来极其离谱且有点不太对，但这是一个很好的夸张。

sentences.en: The whole of the early history of Christianity is incomprehensible without understanding its embeddedness in the Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 如果不理解基督教对罗马帝国的融入，整个早期基督教史就是不可理解的。

sentences.en: That doesn't sound controversial.
sentences.zh: 听起来倒不怎么具有争议。

sentences.en: That just sounds quite reasonable, I think.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这听起来挺合理的。

sentences.en: I think that's absolutely reasonable.
sentences.zh: 我认为这绝对合情合理。

sentences.en: Or there's going to be, you know, there's some bits of the Syriac world which might contest some of this.
sentences.zh: 或者你知道的，有些叙利亚世界的文献可能会对其中一些观点提出异议。

sentences.en: I don't know how many Syriac listeners have been on this podcast, Mary.
sentences.zh: 玛丽，我不知道有多少叙利亚听众听过这个播客。

sentences.en: I will probably get away with it, but you sense that I'm being very careful and covering my back.
sentences.zh: 我大概能蒙混过关，但你能感觉到我非常小心翼翼，在为自己留后路。

sentences.en: I mean, Mary, on that theme of, again, looking at Virgil, looking at Dante, looking at the way the Roman emperors are understood.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，玛丽，就这个主题而言，再次审视维吉尔，审视但丁，审视人们理解罗马皇帝的方式。

sentences.en: I mean, so Dante is identifying with the tradition of the Caesars.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，但丁认同的是凯撒的传统。

sentences.en: He's kind of, he's an enthusiast for the Empire against the papacy.
sentences.zh: 他某种程度上是帝国对抗教皇的热情支持者。

sentences.en: And so when they go down into the lowest pit of hell and they see Satan, he's gnawing on Judas, but he's also gnawing on Brutus and Cassius, who are absolutely, you know, I mean,
sentences.zh: 所以当他们下到地狱的最底层看到撒旦时，撒旦在啃咬犹大，但他也同时在啃咬布鲁图斯和卡西乌斯，而他们绝对，你知道的，我的意思是，

sentences.en: they're up there with the worst people who ever lived for murdering Julius Caesar.
sentences.zh: 他们因为谋杀尤利乌斯·凯撒，与有史以来最恶劣的人同列。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And, you know, so it is, I mean, I think what's interesting, and it's what I hope I bring out in the book,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，所以我觉得有趣的是，这也是我希望在书里展现出来的，

sentences.en: is that these equivalences and this embeddedness is always more complicated.
sentences.zh: 这些对等关系以及这种融入总是更加复杂。

sentences.en: You know, it's always more complicated than it looks.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它总是比看上去要复杂。

sentences.en: And, you know, one way of telling the history of the early church is, of course, to see pagan emperors as great persecutors.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，讲述早期教会历史的一种方式，当然是将异教徒皇帝视为残酷的迫害者。

sentences.en: But there's always another side and there's always another kind of engagement.
sentences.zh: 但凡事总有另一面，也总有另一种形式的交织。

sentences.en: I mean, I think one of the, my favourite objects, it's kind of, it's a bit over the top, is a Transylvanian religious chalice from a cathedral in Transylvania, 16th century,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为我最喜欢的物件之一——有点过于夸张了——是一件来自特兰西瓦尼亚一座大教堂的16世纪、

sentences.en: 17th century, fuzzy date.
sentences.zh: 17世纪的特兰西瓦尼亚宗教圣杯，具体年代有些模糊。

sentences.en: And it's a communion chalice.
sentences.zh: 这是一个圣餐杯。

sentences.en: And what is set in this communion chalice, out of which the faithful are going to drink the blood of Christ and take the bread, what do you see?
sentences.zh: 而镶嵌在这个圣餐杯里的——信徒们将从这里饮用基督的宝血、领受圣饼——你看到了什么？

sentences.en: They've set in it a whole array of Roman coins, including Nero.
sentences.zh: 他们在上面镶嵌了一整排罗马硬币，其中包括尼禄。

sentences.en: So, you know, the kind of the, the image that you have to conjure up for yourself is somebody drinking the communion wine, sipping the communion wine.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，你脑海中必须勾勒出的画面是，有人在饮用圣餐酒，啜饮圣餐酒。

sentences.en: And as they do that, who they brought face to face with?
sentences.zh: 当他们这样做时，他们正与谁面对面？

sentences.en: They're face to face with Nero.
sentences.zh: 他们正与尼禄面对面。

sentences.en: And so these, these figures are kind of operating as a world within which the history of Christianity is being, is being understood.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些人物在某种程度上构成了一个世界，基督教的历史正是在这个世界中被理解的。

sentences.en: And sometimes it is to bring those worlds together, which you have in, with, with your Virgil and Dante example, and with a lot of these, you know,
sentences.zh: 有时是为了将这些世界融合在一起——就像你的维吉尔和但丁的例子中那样，以及在许多这类例子中，

sentences.en: Augustus is always cropping up as, in the context, in art of the birth of Jesus.
sentences.zh: 奥古斯都总是作为背景频繁出现，出现在关于耶稣诞生的艺术作品中。

sentences.en: So you've got, you're saying that these histories go together, and you're also saying these histories are forever in opposition to one another.
sentences.zh: 所以你的意思是，这些历史是交织在一起的，但你同时也认为这些历史永远处于彼此对立之中。

sentences.en: But it's fair to say, is it, Mary, that throughout the history subsequent to the fall of the Western Roman Empire, that Rome in particular has been seen, I mean,
sentences.zh: 不过这样说是否公正呢，玛丽，在西罗马帝国灭亡之后的整个历史中，罗马尤其被视为——我的意思是，

sentences.en: I don't know so much with Greece, but Rome has been seen as synonymous with kind of power and a kind of prestige, right?
sentences.zh: 我对希腊了解不多，但罗马一直被视为权力和某种声望的同义词，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, that's a constant, isn't it, in post-Roman history?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在后罗马时期的历史中，这是一个常态，不是吗？

sentences.en: That's one of the constants.
sentences.zh: 这是常态之一。

sentences.en: Certainly we can really forget Greece here.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们在这里完全可以忽略希腊。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, the rediscovery of Greece was hugely influential, particularly in the 19th century, you know, and you can trace the history of, say,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，希腊的被重新发现具有巨大的影响力，尤其是在19世纪，你知道，你可以追溯比如，

sentences.en: Alexander the Great through some of this period.
sentences.zh: 亚历山大大帝在这段时期的历史。

sentences.en: But essentially, when we're thinking about imagining the ancient world and thinking about how the ancient world impacts on us, then it's Rome.
sentences.zh: 但本质上，当我们构想古代世界并思考古代世界如何影响我们时，那就是罗马。

sentences.en: And it is, it is about power.
sentences.zh: 而且它确实关乎权力。

sentences.en: It's about larger than lifeness, but it's also about corruption.
sentences.zh: 它关乎超越寻常的宏大，但也关乎腐败。

sentences.en: It's about murder.
sentences.zh: 它关乎谋杀。

sentences.en: It's about dynasties going wrong.
sentences.zh: 它关乎误入歧途的王朝。

sentences.en: It's about persecution.
sentences.zh: 它关乎迫害。

sentences.en: It's a very male world, too.
sentences.zh: 这也是一个非常男权的世界。

sentences.en: So that, I mean, that sense that actually what we're talking about in the Middle Ages, if we're looking at the legacy of the classical world, is really Rome.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，那种感觉其实我们在中世纪谈论的——如果我们着眼于古典世界的遗产——确实就是罗马。

sentences.en: I mean, and the extent to which Greece appears, the stories of the Trojan War, the Greek myths.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，至于希腊以何种程度出现，也就是特洛伊战争的故事、希腊神话。

sentences.en: I mean, it's being mediated through Rome.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们是通过罗马来中介传递的。

sentences.en: It's being mediated through Rome.
sentences.zh: 它们是通过罗马来中介传递的。

sentences.en: And the other person that you'd add into the equation, along with Virgil and Dante, is you'll say, look, you know,
sentences.zh: 你会在维吉尔和但丁之外加入方程的另一个人，你会说，看，你知道，

sentences.en: where do people know what we call the Greek myths from at this period?
sentences.zh: 在这个时期，人们是从哪里知道我们所谓的希腊神话的？

sentences.en: Anything from the Middle Ages to the Baroque period, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 我想，从圣经中世纪到巴洛克时期的任何时候都是如此。

sentences.en: Where do they know those?
sentences.zh: 他们是从哪里知道这些的？

sentences.en: Well, mostly they know them through Ovid.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们大多是通过奥维德了解到的。

sentences.en: They are Roman versions of the Greek myth.
sentences.zh: 它们是希腊神话的罗马版本。

sentences.en: And they're always kind of looking, I think, one eye, you know, over the shoulder at what Dominic's talking about, really Roman power, as well as the Roman imagination.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为它们总是带着一种审视的目光，你知道，回过头来看看多米尼克所谈论的内容，也就是真正的罗马权力，以及罗马的想象力。

sentences.en: And they're making kind of different arguments and debates and discussions around it.
sentences.zh: 他们围绕着它展开了各种不同的论点、辩论和讨论。

sentences.en: I think that if the Twelve Caesars, let's say, or any of these images of Roman power had been, you know, utterly,
sentences.zh: 我认为，如果《十二凯萨传》或者任何这些罗马权力的形象，你知道，完全是，

sentences.en: simply rubber stamps of modern political power looking back to antiquity, they wouldn't have had half so much edge.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是对回溯古代的现代政治权力的简单橡皮图章，它们就不会具有一半的影响力。

sentences.en: They wouldn't have had half so much longevity.
sentences.zh: 它们就不会有那么长的生命力。

sentences.en: You know, we'd have got bored.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们会感到厌烦的。

sentences.en: We'd have got really, really bored of them by now.
sentences.zh: 我们到现在对它们真的、真的会感到厌烦的。

sentences.en: But it's because they always raise questions and they're always harder to pin down than you think that they've got such continuing momentum.
sentences.zh: 但正是因为它们总是引发问题，而且比你想象的更难轻易定论，它们才拥有如此持久的势头。

sentences.en: Mary, I've got two questions.
sentences.zh: 玛丽，我有两个问题。

sentences.en: So one is a very boring, small housekeeping question.
sentences.zh: 所以其中一个是关于琐碎日常的无聊小问题。

sentences.en: Is the reason that we think of Hercules rather than Heracles and Shakespeare refers to Jove rather than Zeus, is that just because we're getting all filtered through the Romans?
sentences.zh: 我们想到的是“海格力斯”（Hercules）而不是“赫拉克勒斯”（Heracles），而莎士比亚指的是“朱庇特”（Jove）而不是“宙斯”（Zeus），原因仅仅是因为这一切都经过了罗马人的过滤吗？

sentences.en: That they don't have access to the Greek myths unmediated by the Romans?
sentences.zh: 是因为他们接触不到未经罗马人中介的希腊神话吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's mostly that.
sentences.zh: 是的，主要就是这个原因。

sentences.en: And I think that as soon as you get, and it would start a bit earlier than the late 19th century,
sentences.zh: 我认为，一旦你开始接触到这些——这比19世纪晚期要稍微早一点开始——

sentences.en: but as soon as you get a load of self-conscious Hellenists looking back and saying,
sentences.zh: 但一旦你看到一大群具有自我意识的希腊文化崇拜者回过头来说，

sentences.en: hey, guys, you need to, you know, there's somewhere else to go, then, of course, we get the naming wars.
sentences.zh: 嘿，伙计们，你们需要，你知道的，还有别的地方可去，那么，当然，我们就迎来了命名之争。

sentences.en: And you can tell that in, you know, you can tell that someone who calls Heracles, Heracles is telling you, think Greece.
sentences.zh: 你可以从这一点看出，你知道，你可以看出管赫拉克勒斯叫赫拉克勒斯的人是在告诉你：想想希腊。

sentences.en: Tom Holland is that person.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·霍兰就是那样的人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: OK, so we've got a very good question, much better than my last question from one of our listeners, SO3 Clausewitz.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以我们有一个非常棒的问题，比我上一个问题好得多，来自我们的听众之一，SO3 克劳塞维茨。

sentences.en: And Clausewitz says, and I think this is a fascinating question, was the Renaissance destined to be Greco-Roman?
sentences.zh: 克劳塞维茨说——我认为这是一个迷人的问题——文艺复兴注定是希腊-罗马式的吗？

sentences.en: So he says, basically, is there a counterfactual what if, where it's Egyptian or Persian or whatever, sort of more Eastern?
sentences.zh: 所以他说，基本上，是否存在一种反事实的假设，即它可能是埃及的、波斯的或其他某种更偏东方的风格？

sentences.en: Or was it always bound to be Greco-Roman, I suppose because of the imprints of the Roman Empire on Western Europe?
sentences.zh: 或者它注定是希腊-罗马式的，我猜是因为罗马帝国对西欧留下的印记？

sentences.en: I think that you could say it was almost bound to be, because, you know, we're sitting in a continent and a landmass where we dig in the soil.
sentences.zh: 我想你可以说它几乎是注定如此的，因为，你知道，我们坐落在一个我们在此掘土的大陆和陆地上。

sentences.en: And what do we find?
sentences.zh: 我们发现了什么？

sentences.en: Well, if we're in Italy, we might find busts of Roman emperors.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果我们身在意大利，我们可能会找到罗马皇帝的半身像。

sentences.en: You know, you can be in Durham and we're finding coins with Roman emperors.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你可能身处达勒姆，而我们在那里发现了印有罗马皇帝头像的硬币。

sentences.en: You know, Shakespeare refers to, you know, the imprints of Roman figures on coins.
sentences.zh: 你知道，莎士比亚提到了，你知道，硬币上罗马人物的印记。

sentences.en: But what lies beneath our feet is Roman, really.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，埋藏在我们脚下的东西是罗马的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's not actually Greco-Roman, it's Roman.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它其实不是希腊-罗马的，而是罗马的。

sentences.en: And what I think is, why that question I think is interesting is, of course, it's slightly challenging, the kind of assumption that comes from that.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，为什么我认为这个问题很有趣，当然是因为它稍微挑战了由此产生的某种假设。

sentences.en: You know, the only thing worth studying in antiquity, the only people who've got any brains at all were the Romans and the Greeks.
sentences.zh: 你知道，古代唯一值得研究的事物，唯一有点头脑的人只有罗马人和希腊人。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Now, in fact, we know that it's a much more complicated intellectual world than that, which certainly, for example, and there'd be many others, you know, includes Egypt.
sentences.zh: 现在，事实上，我们知道这是一个比这复杂得多的知识世界，例如，当然还有许多其他文明，你知道，其中就包括埃及。

sentences.en: And both the Greeks and the Romans knew that they had got a lot from Egypt.
sentences.zh: 希腊人和罗马人都知道他们从埃及受益匪浅。

sentences.en: How does Julius Caesar manage to reform the calendar so that it gives us the calendar that we have pretty much today?
sentences.zh: 尤利乌斯·凯撒是如何设法改革日历，从而给我们留下了几乎和今天一模一样的日历的？

sentences.en: Well, he doesn't think of it himself.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这不是他自己想出来的。

sentences.en: He gets some Egyptian boffins on board and they tell him how to reform the calendar.
sentences.zh: 他请来了一些埃及的专家，是他们告诉他如何改革日历的。

sentences.en: So you can't in kind of in my world when I'm teaching, I'm wanting to encourage students to look a little more critically at that kind of, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以在某种程度上，在我的世界里，当我授课时，我想鼓励学生们更具批判性地看待那种，你知道，

sentences.en: total domination of Romano-Greek antiquity, I'll call it.
sentences.zh: 我称之为罗马-希腊古代文化的绝对统治地位。

sentences.en: And to see where it comes from and to see its relationships with the other cultures of the ancient Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 并去看看它是从哪里来的，看看它与古代地中海其他文化之间的关系。

sentences.en: Mary, I mean, with specifically on Egypt, of course, I mean,
sentences.zh: 玛丽，我的意思是，特别谈到埃及，当然，我的意思是，

sentences.en: people were fascinated by Egypt in the Renaissance and they yearned to kind of crack what they thought was the hidden wisdom of the Egyptians.
sentences.zh: 在文艺复兴时期，人们对埃及着迷不已，他们渴望破解他们认为是埃及人隐藏的智慧。

sentences.en: But they couldn't because they couldn't read the text.
sentences.zh: 但他们做不到，因为他们看不懂这些文本。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so the key, I mean, the key to, and of course, the key to the rediscovery of Greece is also the rediscovery of the Greek language and learning the Greek language.
sentences.zh: 所以关键，我的意思是，通往——当然，重新发现希腊的关键也是重新发现希腊语和学习希腊语。

sentences.en: And I guess that we're calling this episode classic.
sentences.zh: 我想我们把这一集叫做“古典”。

sentences.en: So up till now, we've really been looking at, you know, the reception of Greece and Rome.
sentences.zh: 所以到目前为止，我们实际上一直在关注，你知道，希腊和罗马的接受史。

sentences.en: But classics is also particularly about the languages, about Greek and Latin.
sentences.zh: 但古典学（Classics）也特别关乎语言，关乎希腊语和拉丁语。

sentences.en: And I wonder if we should perhaps go for a break now.
sentences.zh: 我想我们现在是不是应该休息一下了。

sentences.en: But after the break, if we could look at the way in which the idea of classics being the study of Greek and Latin and how that's kind of influenced the role.
sentences.zh: 但在休息之后，如果我们能探讨一下古典学作为希腊语和拉丁语研究这一概念，以及它如何影响了这一角色。

sentences.en: I mean, it has a kind of sense that this is a very elite thing to study and all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它带有一种感觉，即这是一门非常精英化的学科，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And I know that you have strong views on that.
sentences.zh: 我知道你对此有强烈的看法。

sentences.en: So perhaps we could come to that after the break.
sentences.zh: 所以也许我们可以在休息之后再讨论这个问题。

sentences.en: Arve, we are looking at classics, the way in which the civilizations of Greece and Rome have been interpreted, reinterpreted over the course of the centuries.
sentences.zh: 阿夫，我们正在关注古典学，关注希腊和罗马文明在几个世纪中被解释、重新解释的方式。

sentences.en: And we have with us none other than Mary Beard, who is professor of classics at Cambridge.
sentences.zh: 我们邀请到了剑桥大学古典学教授玛丽·比尔德（Mary Beard）做客节目。

sentences.en: And Mary, this idea of classics, the joining together of Greek and Latin as a fit subject of study at university.
sentences.zh: 玛丽，古典学这个概念，将希腊语和拉丁语结合起来作为大学里适合研究的学科。

sentences.en: I mean, this has a very kind of lengthy tradition, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这有着非常漫长的传统，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, in Europe, but it kind of takes on a particular contours in England.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在欧洲，但它在英国呈现出了特殊的轮廓。

sentences.en: Yeah, it takes on particular contours in England.
sentences.zh: 是的，它在英国呈现出了特殊的轮廓。

sentences.en: And it would be naive to say that there's been no connection between class and classics, that the learning of Latin in particular, rather less Greek.
sentences.zh: 如果说阶级与古典学之间没有任何联系，拉丁语的学习尤其是这样，希腊语相对少一些——这就太天真了。

sentences.en: Greek has always been a bit more kind of upmarket, recherche, you know.
sentences.zh: 希腊语一直更偏向高端、冷门，你知道的。

sentences.en: A bit bohemian, is it Greek compared to Latin?
sentences.zh: 相比拉丁语，希腊语是不是更具有波西米亚风格？

sentences.en: Slightly more bohemian, yes.
sentences.zh: 稍微更有波西米亚风，是的。

sentences.en: And it's got all kinds of connections with some things that we don't much like.
sentences.zh: 它与我们不太喜欢的某些事物有着各种各样的联系。

sentences.en: You know, Athenian democracy was not terribly the flavour of the month in the early 19th century, for example.
sentences.zh: 你知道，例如，在19世纪初期，雅典民主并不是特别受人欢迎。

sentences.en: And so we're seeing it through Rome and we're seeing an elitism here.
sentences.zh: 所以我们是通过罗马来审视它的，我们在这里看到了精英主义。

sentences.en: And also up to a point, we're seeing the acquisition of Latin as a gatekeeper to elite culture here.
sentences.zh: 而且在某种程度上，我们也看到掌握拉丁语成了通往精英文化的把关人。

sentences.en: OK, so we have a question from Andrew here.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以我们这里有一个来自安德鲁的问题。

sentences.en: What is it about studying the classics that seems to appeal to the elite?
sentences.zh: 为什么研究古典学似乎对精英们有着极大的吸引力？

sentences.en: Well, I would say almost nothing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我会说几乎毫无吸引力。

sentences.en: I mean, I think that one of the points about what, let's say, the English elite studied in the 18th and early 19th century,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为，18世纪和19世纪初的英国精英们所研究的东西中的一个关键点在于，

sentences.en: was that they studied Latin and Greek.
sentences.zh: 他们研究的是拉丁语和希腊语。

sentences.en: They studied language.
sentences.zh: 他们研究的是语言。

sentences.en: And what did they spend most of their time doing?
sentences.zh: 他们把大部分时间都花在做什么上？

sentences.en: Well, they were translating Shakespeare into Latin.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们在把莎士比亚翻译成拉丁语。

sentences.en: They were translating Milton into Latin.
sentences.zh: 他们在把弥尔顿翻译成拉丁语。

sentences.en: And part of the point of this, and I think once you can't really emphasise this too strongly,
sentences.zh: 而这其中的部分意义——我认为一旦你领会了这一点，怎么强调都不为过——

sentences.en: they weren't much.
sentences.zh: 他们读得并不多。

sentences.en: They were reading Virgil, but they weren't thinking about Virgil as a literary text.
sentences.zh: 他们在读维吉尔，但他们并不是把维吉尔当作文学文本来思考。

sentences.en: They were thinking about how they wrote like Virgil.
sentences.zh: 他们在思考如何像维吉尔那样写作。

sentences.en: And one of the kind of bizarre things and one of the things that made the learning of Latin so good as a gatekeeper to elite culture was it was also in many ways so pointless.
sentences.zh: 其中一件诡异的事情，也是让拉丁语学习成为精英文化把关人的绝佳途径的原因，在于它在许多方面也毫无用处。

sentences.en: You know, they were not...
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们并没有……

sentences.en: So the pointlessness is the point.
sentences.zh: 所以毫无用处恰恰就是它的用处。

sentences.en: Pointlessness is the point.
sentences.zh: 毫无用处就是它的用处。

sentences.en: You are learning absolute fluency in a dead language.
sentences.zh: 你正在学习一门死语言的绝对流利度。

sentences.en: Now, they were not...
sentences.zh: 现在，他们并没有……

sentences.en: They were a bit, but they were not much, certainly not at school and not a lot at university.
sentences.zh: 他们懂一点，但并不多，肯定不在学校里，在大学里也不多。

sentences.en: They were not thinking about the literary merit of the Aeneid.
sentences.zh: 他们没有去思考《埃涅阿斯纪》的文学价值。

sentences.en: They weren't thinking much about, let's say, Roman philosophy.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有过多地思考，比如说，罗马哲学。

sentences.en: They weren't reading Cicero in order to think about how you organised a state.
sentences.zh: 他们阅读西塞罗不是为了思考如何组织一个国家。

sentences.en: The big, real focus of their learning was translating English into Latin.
sentences.zh: 他们学习的核心焦点是将英语翻译成拉丁语。

sentences.en: And we now think of classics as a subject, and I'm happy to say it is very much now in the modern world, as a subject which is about the Greeks and Romans.
sentences.zh: 我们现在把古典学视为一门学科，我很高兴地说，它在现代世界中非常重要，是一门关于希腊人和罗马人的学科。

sentences.en: You have a...
sentences.zh: 你有一种……

sentences.en: You access it through language, often, not always.
sentences.zh: 通常——并非总是——你是通过语言来接触它的。

sentences.en: But it's about that kind of culture.
sentences.zh: 但它是关于那种文化的。

sentences.en: I think if we'd gone back to the late 18th century, we wouldn't recognise what these people were doing.
sentences.zh: 我想如果我们回到18世纪末，我们根本无法认同这些人在做什么。

sentences.en: Mary, what's about this argument that's a bit...
sentences.zh: 玛丽，关于这个有点……的争论是怎么回事？

sentences.en: I know Tom's got a question about Thomas Hobbes, but I want to jump in before that.
sentences.zh: 我知道汤姆有个关于托马斯·霍布斯的问题，但我想在此之前插话。

sentences.en: Oh, God.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: I always pass on Thomas Hobbes' questions.
sentences.zh: 我总是跳过关于托马斯·霍布斯的问题。

sentences.en: So my question is, there's a slightly, what seems to me, a slightly crude way of thinking that people learn, do classics because they want to be, because of empire.
sentences.zh: 所以我的问题是，人们学习古典学，是因为他们想成为、因为帝国——在我看来，这种想法似乎有点、稍微有些粗糙。

sentences.en: Because they want to, purely because they want, they would be imperialists.
sentences.zh: 因为他们纯粹是因为想这样做，他们会成为帝国主义者。

sentences.en: And they think, is that right?
sentences.zh: 他们在想，是这样吗？

sentences.en: I think it's half right.
sentences.zh: 我认为这说对了一半。

sentences.en: Most of these kind of stereotypes that we have about why and how the classics were studied in, let's say, 19th century, 18th century, they're always half true.
sentences.zh: 我们对19世纪、18世纪为什么以及如何研究古典学的绝大多数刻板印象，总是一半是对的。

sentences.en: And there is no doubt that some people who were avowed imperialists saw the Roman Empire as their lodestar, really,
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，一些公开的帝国主义者确实把罗马帝国视为他们的北极星，

sentences.en: that Britain had taken on the mantle of ancient Rome and was, in a sense, replicating and doing better than the Romans.
sentences.zh: 认为英国继承了古罗马的衣钵，并在某种程度上复制并超越了罗马人。

sentences.en: And, but I think it's more complicated than that.
sentences.zh: 但是，我认为事情比这更复杂。

sentences.en: I mean, partly the relationship between the Roman Empire and the British Empire was always a very fragile one.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，部分原因在于罗马帝国与大英帝国之间的关系一直非常脆弱。

sentences.en: And I think you can see that if you go to the famous statue of Boudiccaire or Boudiccaire.
sentences.zh: 我想如果你去看布狄卡（Boudicca）或布狄卡（Boudicca）的那座著名雕塑，你就会发现这一点。

sentences.en: Tom loves this.
sentences.zh: 汤姆喜欢这个。

sentences.en: Tom's always saying this to me.
sentences.zh: 汤姆总是对我说这个。

sentences.en: We've done a whole thing on this.
sentences.zh: 我们已经就此做过一整期节目了。

sentences.en: Oh, brilliant.
sentences.zh: 哦，太棒了。

sentences.en: Well, you go to that statue and you look at what's written underneath.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你去那座雕塑前，看看下面写着什么。

sentences.en: You know, here we've got, you know, a big rebel against Rome, standing up for the native Brits against imperial oppression.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这里我们有一个反对罗马的伟大叛逆者，为了本土英国人对抗帝国的压迫而站出来。

sentences.en: And the poem that is the Cooper poem that's written by her, underneath her, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且那首库珀（Cooper）的诗，写在她的雕塑下方，你知道的，

sentences.en: says words to the effect of, don't worry, Boudicca, your descendants will rule more of the world than the Romans did.
sentences.zh: 大意是说，别担心，布狄卡，你的后代统治的世界将比罗马人还要广阔。

sentences.en: It's basically the message.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是传达的信息。

sentences.en: I love that.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个。

sentences.en: So, so whose side are we on here?
sentences.zh: 那么，那么我们到底站在哪一边？

sentences.en: And Mary also, I mean, it's, it's not just in Britain, is it?
sentences.zh: 而且玛丽，我的意思是，这、这不仅发生在英国，对吧？

sentences.en: Because in France, I mean, France, you know, they're using, in Algeria, they, they, the French see themselves as kind of the heirs of Rome,
sentences.zh: 因为在法国，我的意思是，法国，你知道的，他们在阿尔及利亚使用着——法国人认为自己是罗马的某种继承人，

sentences.en: bringing civilisation and baths and things to the desert wild.
sentences.zh: 给沙漠荒野带来了文明、浴场和各种事物。

sentences.en: But simultaneously, they're bunging up a statue of Vercingetorix to mark the defeated.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，他们却竖起了一尊韦尔金盖托里克斯的雕塑来纪念失败者。

sentences.en: And the Germans are doing the same with Arminius, who's defeated.
sentences.zh: 德国人对待战败的阿米尼乌斯也是如此。

sentences.en: That is, that is absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 那是，那是绝对正确的。

sentences.en: So even with that broad equivalence between Rome and modern empires, there's always that.
sentences.zh: 因此，即使在罗马与现代帝国之间存在着那种广泛的对等关系，这一点也始终存在。

sentences.en: So, you know, who's coming out on top?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，谁才是最后的赢家？

sentences.en: Who's really like whom?
sentences.zh: 谁才真正像谁？

sentences.en: I think also we tend to forget that Rome gave people a language for critiquing empire.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们也往往忘记了，罗马为人们提供了一种批判帝国的语言。

sentences.en: Well, exactly.
sentences.zh: 嗯，确实如此。

sentences.en: And that seems to me hugely important.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这极其重要。

sentences.en: You know, there were some of these, you know, some of these boys, there were boys at Oxford nipping off to, to quotes.
sentences.zh: 你知道，其中一些人，你知道，牛津有些小伙子急急忙忙地去引经据典。

sentences.en: And I'll put all this in inverted commas, quotes, rule India.
sentences.zh: 我会把这一切加上引号，引经据典地说，去统治印度。

sentences.en: Others were going up to work on the Manchester Guardian to say what an absolute pile of shite imperialism was.
sentences.zh: 其他人则去《曼彻斯特卫报》工作，宣称帝国主义绝对是一堆狗屎。

sentences.en: And they'd all learned it from the classics.
sentences.zh: 而他们都是从古典学中学到这一点的。

sentences.en: But Mary, just before that, the reason I just wanted to mention Hobbes was that he famously,
sentences.zh: 但是玛丽，就在那之前，我之所以想提及霍布斯，是因为他曾有一句名言：

sentences.en: after the execution of Charles I said, people should not be reading Greek and Latin history, because it just encourages them to kill, you know, their rightful kings.
sentences.zh: 在查理一世被处决后，他说人们不应该阅读希腊和罗马的历史，因为这只会怂恿他们去杀死，你知道的，他们合法的国王。

sentences.en: You know, they're tyrannicides and things.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们成了弑君者之类的人。

sentences.en: It's terrible behaviour.
sentences.zh: 这是可怕的行为。

sentences.en: You know, it's got to be stamped out.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这必须被坚决根除。

sentences.en: And both the American revolutionaries and the French revolutionaries were absolutely steeped in the classical world.
sentences.zh: 无论是美国革命者还是法国革命者，都深深浸淫于古典世界之中。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So it is also about, you know, it kind of underpins revolution, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以它也关乎，你知道的，它某种程度上支撑了革命，不是吗？

sentences.en: I have been banging on about this for more years than I like to think, you know, that there isn't inherent politics in the classical world.
sentences.zh: 我已经喋喋不休地谈论这个好多年了，超过了我愿意去想的年头，你知道的，古典世界中并不存在什么内生的政治倾向。

sentences.en: You can use and you do use classical examples, classical tropes, classical cliches to justify revolution as much as to justify oppression.
sentences.zh: 你既可以使用、也确实在使用古典时代的例子、古典时代的意象、古典时代的陈词滥调来为革命辩护，就像为压迫辩护一样。

sentences.en: And, you know, the classics has got a, you know, it's got a pretty kind of poor record when it comes to underpinning European dictatorship.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，当涉及到支撑欧洲独裁统治时，古典学的记录，你知道，相当糟糕。

sentences.en: You know, Mussolini is the start.
sentences.zh: 你知道，墨索里尼就是个开始。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: But it's also got a, in my view, others might disagree, it's got a pretty fine record in asking people to critique imperial power, critique corruption.
sentences.zh: 但在我看来——其他人可能会有不同看法——它在要求人们批判帝国权力、批判腐败方面，有着相当出色的记录。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't see really how you can read, even if you're not reading it for its history.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不明白你怎么能去阅读——即使你不是为了它的历史而读。

sentences.en: How can you study the Roman historian Tacitus and not come away with a countercultural version about autocracy, one man rule and the corruption of empire?
sentences.zh: 你怎么能研究罗马历史学家塔西陀，却不从中得出一种关于专制、一人统治以及帝国腐败的反对主流文化的看法呢？

sentences.en: And indeed empire.
sentences.zh: 确实还有帝国本身。

sentences.en: Well, even beyond that, though, I mean, Tom and I were talking about this before we started the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，甚至不仅于此，汤姆和我录播客前还在谈论这个。

sentences.en: And I said to him that the two best known popular modern versions of the Roman Empire, so there are Claudius and the film Gladiator.
sentences.zh: 我对他说，关于罗马帝国最著名的两部现代大众版本作品，也就是克劳迪斯和电影《角斗士》。

sentences.en: And in both, there's a narrative device where one character wants to bring back the Republic.
sentences.zh: 在这两部作品中，都有一个叙事设定：一个角色想要恢复共和国。

sentences.en: He says, we're corrupt, we're autocratic, we're repressive.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们已经腐败了，我们专制了，我们压迫了。

sentences.en: You know, we need so.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们需要……

sentences.en: So even in our sort of modern retellings of Rome, that stuff is woven in.
sentences.zh: 所以，即使在我们对罗马的现代重述中，这些东西也已经被编织进去了。

sentences.en: We, we, we can't ever, you can't ever tell Rome or you tell a very, very uninteresting story of Rome if you didn't keep that, that side, that other side on board.
sentences.zh: 我们、我们、我们永远无法——如果你不把那一面、把那另一面考虑进去，你讲述罗马的故事就会非常、非常无趣。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, look, for me, when did I first really see that Latin could speak for me?
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，你看，对我来说，我第一次真正看到拉丁语能为我发声是在什么时候？

sentences.en: It was when I read Tacitus and it was the biography, not his main histories of, of the early Roman Empire, but his biography of his father-in-law, Agricola.
sentences.zh: 那是我读塔西陀的时候，读的不是他关于早期罗马帝国的正史，而是他为岳父阿古利可拉写的传记。

sentences.en: And, you know, I was a sort of disaffected lefty teenager.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我曾是一个心怀不满的左翼叛逆青少年。

sentences.en: And I'd sort of fetched up learning Latin because they thought that's what brainy girls did.
sentences.zh: 我阴差阳错地学起了拉丁语，因为他们觉得聪明女孩就该这么做。

sentences.en: And we were reading Tacitus' biography of Agricola and then I came across the bit where Tacitus puts into the mouth, admittedly, of, you know, a native Brit,
sentences.zh: 当时我们正在读塔西陀写的《阿古利可拉传》，然后我遇到了这样一段：塔西陀借一个英国本土人之口——尽管这个本土人从未说过这话——

sentences.en: though the native Brit never said it.
sentences.zh: 虽然这个本土人从未说过这话。

sentences.en: He rallies the opposition to Rome by saying, what do the Romans do?
sentences.zh: 他号召人们反抗罗马，说道：罗马人做了什么？

sentences.en: They make a desert and call it peace.
sentences.zh: 他们制造了一片荒凉，却称之为和平。

sentences.en: And that was when my eyes sort of opened because I thought there are people in the Roman world who were talking to me about, about me.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，我的双眼仿佛睁开了，因为我想，罗马世界里有人在跟我说话，谈论着我。

sentences.en: You know, they're not just sitting there yomping across Gaul, you know, on a, on a kind of pledge of massacring the poor natives.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们不只是坐在那里，在对屠杀穷苦本地人的某种承诺下，在高卢境内横冲直撞。

sentences.en: They're, they're thinking about what empire is.
sentences.zh: 他们在思考什么是帝国。

sentences.en: And, you know, actually, if you, if you were to say, you know, has there ever been a better critique of empire than they make a desert and call it peace?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，事实上，如果你要问，你知道，是否曾有过比“他们制造了一片荒凉，却称之为和平”更好的对帝国的批判？

sentences.en: You know, I, I think Tacitus wins hands down, at least on, um, succinctness and lucidity.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为塔西陀稳操胜券，至少在简洁和明晰度上是这样的。

sentences.en: Um, well, kind of on that, a slight angle to that, that we've got a question from Murph Man, a.k.a.
sentences.zh: 嗯，顺着这个话题，从一个稍微不同的角度切入，我们收到了一个来自“墨夫男”（Murph Man）也就是贾斯汀·墨菲（Justin Murphy）的问题，

sentences.en: Justin Murphy, who asks, and I think this is a really interesting question.
sentences.zh: 他问道，我认为这是一个非常有趣的问题。

sentences.en: Have classicists traditionally downplayed, and do they still, the cruelty and unfairness of the Roman world?
sentences.zh: 传统上，古典学者是否一直在淡化，并且现在是否仍在淡化罗马世界的残酷与不公？

sentences.en: And if so, why?
sentences.zh: 如果是这样，为什么？

sentences.en: I mean, that is a quite an interesting question.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个相当有趣的问题。

sentences.en: Does the, does, classicists inevitably are kind of passionate about the need to study, you know, the literature, the languages of these ancient peoples.
sentences.zh: 古典学者是否不可避免地对研究这些古代人民的文学和语言有一种热情？

sentences.en: Does, does kind of emphasising, you know, the wonder of Virgil or Homer or whatever, lead people to downplay the costs of what Greece and Rome meant for people?
sentences.zh: 强调维吉尔或荷马等人的伟大，是否会导致人们淡化希腊和罗马对人们所造成的代价？

sentences.en: I mean, I hope I haven't, you know.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我希望我没有，你知道的。

sentences.en: No, absolutely, you haven't.
sentences.zh: 不，当然，你没有。

sentences.en: But I just wonder, the tradition, is this a problem with the tradition?
sentences.zh: 但我只是在想，这种传统，这是传统的一个问题吗？

sentences.en: I think there is a degree of a problem with tradition.
sentences.zh: 我认为传统在某种程度上确实存在问题。

sentences.en: Look, you know, there's, throughout my career, you know, I've been reading people like Moses Finlay or E.R.
sentences.zh: 看，你知道，在我的整个职业生涯中，你知道，我一直在读像摩西·芬利（Moses Finley）或E.R.道兹（E.R. Dodds）这样的人的书，

sentences.en: Dodds, you know, who are looking the classical world in the eye and always have done.
sentences.zh: 他们直面古典世界，并且一直以来都是如此。

sentences.en: And I think you can go back to the 19th century too, and you can find writers doing the same.
sentences.zh: 我想你也可以追溯到19世纪，你也能发现作家们在做同样的事情。

sentences.en: I think to some extent, there can be a fudge, as much in popular writing as in academic writing, from saying this culture is extremely interesting,
sentences.zh: 我认为在某种程度上，无论是在通俗写作还是在学术写作中，都可能存在一种含糊其辞的倾向，即把“这种文化极其有趣”，

sentences.en: to saying this culture is admirable.
sentences.zh: 偷换成“这种文化令人钦佩”。

sentences.en: And then, tending to downplay things like the treatment of women, slavery, and, or sexual violence, if you like.
sentences.zh: 然后，往往会淡化诸如对待女性的方式、奴隶制、或者说性暴力之类的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, it's certainly the case that when I was at school, and a bit when I was at university, we would read Ovid's Metamorphoses.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，确实在我上学的时候，以及在大学时的一段时间里，我们会阅读奥维德的《变形记》。

sentences.en: Now, my young students now see Ovid's Metamorphoses, interesting as it is, as a work of literature, which is basically a handbook of rape.
sentences.zh: 现在，我年轻的学生们把奥维德的《变形记》——尽管它很有趣——看作是一部文学作品，基本上就是一本强奸手册。

sentences.en: It's one rape after the next.
sentences.zh: 里面是一场接一场的强奸。

sentences.en: And in some ways, that's true.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，确实如此。

sentences.en: We never talked about it like that.
sentences.zh: 我们以前可从不那样谈论它。

sentences.en: I mean, we had that wonderful word, rapture.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们当时用过那个美妙的词，狂喜（rapture）。

sentences.en: This was a rapture, it wasn't a rape.
sentences.zh: 这是狂喜，不是强奸。

sentences.en: And that went hand in hand with...
sentences.zh: 这与……相辅相成。

sentences.en: It's a way of seeing the gods, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这是一种看待神灵的方式，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's a way of seeing the gods, you know.
sentences.zh: 这是一种看待神灵的方式，你知道的。

sentences.en: And, of course, we can, you know.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们可以，你知道的。

sentences.en: What price do you want to pay?
sentences.zh: 你想付出什么代价？

sentences.en: I mean, it's kind of only an explanation, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这也许只是一种解释。

sentences.en: Ask Semele.
sentences.zh: 去问问塞墨勒（Semele）。

sentences.en: Ask Semele, you know.
sentences.zh: 去问问塞墨勒，你知道的。

sentences.en: Is there a downside to seeing the gods?
sentences.zh: 以那种方式看待神灵难道有什么负面影响吗？

sentences.en: Well, yes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有的。

sentences.en: You know, what is Ovid saying about what the costs are of that?
sentences.zh: 你知道，奥维德对这背后的代价作出了怎样的评价？

sentences.en: But I think you could find that outside sexual violence.
sentences.zh: 但我认为你在性暴力之外也能发现这一点。

sentences.en: But, you know, I think there was a tradition of seeing slavery as a bit in the model of, you know, country house servants.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我认为过去有一种传统，把奴隶制视为乡村宅邸仆人的翻版。

sentences.en: Upstairs, downstairs.
sentences.zh: 楼上楼下。

sentences.en: Upstairs, downstairs.
sentences.zh: 楼上楼下。

sentences.en: It's Downton Abbey.
sentences.zh: 这就是《唐顿庄园》。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, you know, the truth is that some of it probably was like that.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，事实是其中一部分可能确实如此。

sentences.en: And those are the bits we know about beSt.
sentences.zh: 而这些正是我们最了解的部分。

sentences.en: You know, the faithful slave of Cicero who gets freed and, you know, and remains a friend of the old master.
sentences.zh: 你知道，西塞罗那个忠诚的奴隶，后来获得自由，你知道的，并且与老主人保持着朋友关系。

sentences.en: Very nostalgic, euphemising version of slavery.
sentences.zh: 非常怀旧、非常美化版本的奴隶制。

sentences.en: Not entirely wrong in some cases.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下并非完全错误。

sentences.en: And what didn't we look at?
sentences.zh: 那我们没有看到的是什么？

sentences.en: We didn't look at agricultural slaves, slaves in factories, slaves in the mines.
sentences.zh: 我们没有看到农业奴隶、工厂里的奴隶、矿井里的奴隶。

sentences.en: We didn't look at the sex slaves.
sentences.zh: 我们没有看到性奴隶。

sentences.en: Yes, who would be castrated or blinded in an eye.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们会被阉割或刺瞎一只眼睛。

sentences.en: I mean, how idiots.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，真是荒唐。

sentences.en: You know this story, Tom, but I'm going to tell it for your listeners.
sentences.zh: 你知道这个故事，汤姆，但我还是要讲给你的听众听。

sentences.en: You know, there's the story of the Emperor Hadrian who gets mad at a slave and blinds him in one eye and then feels terribly remorseful and so says to the slave,
sentences.zh: 你知道，有个故事讲的是哈德良皇帝对一个奴隶生气的奴隶，刺瞎了他的一只眼睛，随后感到无比内疚，于是对奴隶说，

sentences.en: please let me recompense you.
sentences.zh: 请让我补偿你。

sentences.en: Let me buy a present.
sentences.zh: 让我买一件礼物吧。

sentences.en: And what would you like?
sentences.zh: 你想要什么？

sentences.en: And the slave says, my eye back, please.
sentences.zh: 奴隶说，请把我的眼睛还给我。

sentences.en: So, Mary, let me ask you a question, allied to that, about slavery and violence.
sentences.zh: 所以，玛丽，让我问你一个与之相关的问题，关于奴隶制和暴力。

sentences.en: The most famous, I mean, I know you've written about this, the most celebrated Roman monument probably in the world, the place that everybody goes to when they visit Rome,
sentences.zh: 最著名的——我知道你写过关于这个的文章——世界上可能最著名的罗马古迹，每个人去罗马参观时都会去的地方，

sentences.en: the place where children line up to pose with swords and to dress in the costumes.
sentences.zh: 孩子们排队拿着剑摆姿势、穿上戏服的地方。

sentences.en: I believe Sandbrook Jr.
sentences.zh: 我相信小桑德布鲁克（Sandbrook Jr.）

sentences.en: is in that arena.
sentences.zh: 就在那个竞技场里。

sentences.en: He's going there for the half term, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他期中假要去那里，对吧？

sentences.en: He is going there for the half term and we've got it penciled in.
sentences.zh: 他期中假就要去那里，我们已经把它列入计划了。

sentences.en: So, the Coliseum, Gladiators, this is part of that, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以，罗马斗兽场，角斗士，这也是其中的一部分，对吧？

sentences.en: Do you think, do you find, if you are driving past, do you find that distasteful and wrong?
sentences.zh: 你觉得，当你开车路过时，你觉得那令人反感且错误吗？

sentences.en: I don't warm to the idea of gladiatorial display.
sentences.zh: 我对角斗表演这种想法并无好感。

sentences.en: I hope it tells us a little bit about ourselves, because when Sandbrook Jr.
sentences.zh: 我希望这能让我们稍微了解一下我们自己，因为当小桑德布鲁克

sentences.en: lines up and has his photograph taken with the dress-up gladiators, I hope, I'm sure you point out to him, Dominic, that he's invested in that kind of violence and culture.
sentences.zh: 排好队，和那些装扮成角斗士的人拍照时，我希望——我确信你一定向他指出过，多米尼克——他参与了那种暴力与文化。

sentences.en: I'm constantly interrogating violent practices in my episode.
sentences.zh: 我在自己的那一集里不断地审视暴力行为。

sentences.en: And I think that, you know, the Romans are horrible.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，你知道，罗马人是可怕的。

sentences.en: And one of the reasons we study them is because they are horrible.
sentences.zh: 我们研究他们的原因之一，就是因为他们很可怕。

sentences.en: And, you know, they themselves wonder what they are doing, sitting down and, you know, supposedly enjoying the slaughter of human beings.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他们自己也在纳闷，为什么他们会坐在这里，据说是津津有味地欣赏对人类的屠杀。

sentences.en: You know, they're not, we picture them as just a lustful crowd and, you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们并非——我们把他们想象成只是一群嗜血的暴民，而且，你知道，

sentences.en: some of them are and some of them aren't and some of them are both a lustful crowd and a questioning crowd about what's going on.
sentences.zh: 他们当中有些人是，有些人不是，有些人既是嗜血的暴民，也是对正在发生的事情充满质疑的旁观者。

sentences.en: But I think that we have to reflect a little bit on why we so like that site.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们必须稍微反思一下，为什么我们如此喜欢那个场景。

sentences.en: So, yeah, we find distasteful, but we're so invested in that site.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我们觉得恶心，但我们又如此深陷其中。

sentences.en: I mean, gladiator has its cake and eats it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，《角斗士》这部电影真是鱼与熊掌兼得。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, you know, I suspect we have our cake and eat it and the Romans had their cake and eat it.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我怀疑我们是鱼与熊掌兼得，罗马人也是鱼与熊掌兼得。

sentences.en: I think that we also have to remember that it's there's been different versions of how we take that on board over the last few hundred years.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们还必须记住，在过去几百年里，对于我们如何接受这一遗产，曾有过不同的版本。

sentences.en: Because, you know, if we were in the middle of the 19th century and visited Rome, the Colosseum was then still basically a shrine to dead, to martyred Christians.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，如果我们身处19世纪中期并访问罗马，当时的罗马斗兽场基本上仍然是死难殉道基督徒的神龛。

sentences.en: And it was totally overgrown, extremely romantic.
sentences.zh: 而且那里杂草丛生，极其富有浪漫色彩。

sentences.en: Great big cross.
sentences.zh: 立着一个巨大的十字架。

sentences.en: A great big cross.
sentences.zh: 一个巨大的十字架。

sentences.en: The cross is still there, but nobody notices it.
sentences.zh: 那个十字架现在还在，只是没有人注意到它。

sentences.en: And there was a little hermit in his hermitage, you know, in one side of the kind of overgrown garden.
sentences.zh: 在那个杂草丛生的花园的一侧，你知道，有一个隐士住在他的隐修室里。

sentences.en: That's the classiest hermitage in the world, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 那是世界上最高级的隐修室，对吧？

sentences.en: Can you imagine a classiest hermitage?
sentences.zh: 你能想象出更高级的隐修室吗？

sentences.en: And if you said Colosseum then, it's about the persecution of the Christians.
sentences.zh: 如果你当时说起斗兽场，那就是在谈论对基督徒的迫害。

sentences.en: And, of course, you go back to the reason why, you know, why was the Colosseum built in the first place?
sentences.zh: 当然，如果你追溯原因，你知道，斗兽场当初为什么要建造？

sentences.en: Well, there's two reasons for that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这有两个原因。

sentences.en: One is it was built by the new dynasty under Vespasian to obliterate part of the extravagant palace that the Emperor Nero had built.
sentences.zh: 一个是由韦斯帕芗领导的新王朝建造它，为了抹去尼禄皇帝建造的那个奢侈宫殿的一部分。

sentences.en: The Golden House, is it?
sentences.zh: 就是金宫，对吧？

sentences.en: The Golden House.
sentences.zh: 金宫。

sentences.en: And the Colosseum is built on the site of Nero's ornamental lake.
sentences.zh: 斗兽场就建在尼禄的观赏湖遗址上。

sentences.en: And it was a kind of quasi-democratic gesture.
sentences.zh: 这是一种近乎民主的姿态。

sentences.en: It was saying, this used to be the private pleasure grounds of a tyrant.
sentences.zh: 它是在说，这曾经是一个暴君的私人游乐场。

sentences.en: And me, Vespasian, I am giving it back to public entertainment.
sentences.zh: 而我，韦斯帕芗，我把它还给公众娱乐。

sentences.en: It's like politicians playing football, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 就像政客们踢足球一样，对吧？

sentences.en: In a way, in a way.
sentences.zh: 某种程度上，某种程度上。

sentences.en: But, you know, just also remember the other kind of awkward side.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，也要记住另一个尴尬的方面。

sentences.en: How did Vespasian get the money to build this?
sentences.zh: 韦斯帕芗是从哪儿弄到钱来建这个的？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, you know, very expensive piece of work.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，这是一项非常昂贵的工程。

sentences.en: He got it because of his and his sons' put down of the Jewish rebellion just before he took power in 69.
sentences.zh: 他之所以有钱，是因为他和他的儿子们在69年他掌权前不久镇压了犹太叛乱。

sentences.en: And his destruction of the temple.
sentences.zh: 并且摧毁了圣殿。

sentences.en: Mary, just the thought about this kind of idea that perhaps we as a society generally perhaps don't engage with the brutality that underpins so much of, I guess,
sentences.zh: 玛丽，我只是在想这样一种观点：也许我们作为整个社会，往往没有去正视支撑着如此之多——我猜特别是罗马文明的——

sentences.en: particularly Roman civilization.
sentences.zh: 那种残暴本质。

sentences.en: And I wonder if it's to do with the fact that most of us study it when we're children.
sentences.zh: 我在想，这是否与我们大多数人在孩童时期就研究它有关？

sentences.en: It's a topic, you know, it's the childhood of Europe, perhaps therefore it's appropriate to children.
sentences.zh: 这是一个主题，你知道，这是欧洲的童年，所以也许它适合儿童。

sentences.en: And, you know, the thing that I always have to struggle against is the influence of Asterix, in which Julius Caesar conquers Gaul without killing a single person.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我总是不得不与之作斗争的事情，就是《高卢英雄历险记》的影响，在那里，尤利乌斯·凯撒征服高卢时竟然没有杀死一个人。

sentences.en: And, you know, and in which the Gauls are total sweeties.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，里面的高卢人简直是绝对的小甜心。

sentences.en: Well, they're all sweeties, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们全都是小甜心，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, you know.
sentences.zh: 对，你知道的。

sentences.en: And in fact, we wouldn't much like living in ancient Gaul.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们其实并不会很想生活在古代高卢。

sentences.en: No, an indomitable village.
sentences.zh: 没错，一个坚不可摧的村庄。

sentences.en: It'd be terrible.
sentences.zh: 那会糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: No, but absolutely terrible.
sentences.zh: 不，绝对糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: But I think there is that.
sentences.zh: 但我认为确实有这种现象。

sentences.en: It is a kind of, you know, there's a certain infantilization that we have of the ancient world.
sentences.zh: 这是一种，你知道，我们对古代世界存在某种程度的幼稚化倾向。

sentences.en: You know, a projection of, you know, the nuclear family and we've got them all dressed up in their toke as, you know, wife, faithful slave and husband and wife and two kids.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一种投射，你知道，比如核心家庭，我们把他们都穿上托加长袍，扮演着妻子、忠实的奴隶、丈夫以及两个孩子。

sentences.en: But there's also, I think, a little bit of a sanctimonious self-righteousness about it.
sentences.zh: 但我也认为，这里面还有一点虚伪的自以为是。

sentences.en: I mean, and I think that's the other side of our discussions of slavery,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为这是我们讨论奴隶制的另一个方面，

sentences.en: because you take students around slave quarters that you can identify in some Roman houses or Hadrian's great palace at Tivoli outside Rome.
sentences.zh: 因为你带学生参观你在一些罗马房屋或罗马城外蒂沃利的哈德良大宫殿中能够辨认出的奴隶住处时，

sentences.en: And they are terrible, dank, dingy workhouses, really.
sentences.zh: 那些地方其实是可怕、阴暗、昏暗的作坊。

sentences.en: And even with clever students, you can often say to them, would we do that now?
sentences.zh: 即使面对聪明的学生，你经常也可以对他们说：我们现在还会那样做吗？

sentences.en: Oh, no, no, no, no, no, no, we wouldn't.
sentences.zh: 哦，不，不，不，不，不，不，我们不会的。

sentences.en: You know, we don't have slaves.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们没有奴隶。

sentences.en: Well, it's convenient for us to imagine we don't have slaves.
sentences.zh: 好吧，想象我们没有奴隶对我们来说很方便。

sentences.en: But, you know, think where your smartphone's made.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，想想你的智能手机是在哪里制造的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And in what conditions.
sentences.zh: 是在什么环境下制造的。

sentences.en: And, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，

sentences.en: so I think that our relationship of investment in the ancient world is always combined with a sense of certain kind of self-righteousness about how much better we are.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，我们对古代世界的投入关系，总是与一种自以为我们好多少的自以为是感结合在一起。

sentences.en: We are better.
sentences.zh: 我们确实更好。

sentences.en: You know, I'm not going to take I'm not going to take a trip back to ancient Rome if you paid me a very, you know, you know, it's not going to like.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你就算付我再多钱，我也绝不会——你知道的——回到古代罗马去，我可不喜欢那样。

sentences.en: Not even if you were going to be an emphress.
sentences.zh: 即使你是去做女皇也不行吗？

sentences.en: Or maybe, especially not an emphress.
sentences.zh: 或者也许，特别是不去做女皇。

sentences.en: So you end up on an island or something.
sentences.zh: 所以你最后会被流放到一个岛上什么的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm a celebrity, get me out of ancient Rome, you know.
sentences.zh: 对啊，我是个名人，快把我从古罗马救出去吧，你知道的。

sentences.en: Great show that would be.
sentences.zh: 那一定会是个很棒的节目。

sentences.en: But we have to see that there's a complexity here in our engagement.
sentences.zh: 但我们必须看到，我们与它的接触中存在着复杂性。

sentences.en: And we tend to think about these things in very binary terMs.
sentences.zh: 而我们往往倾向于用非常二元的术语来思考这些事情。

sentences.en: Well, Mary, this raises some really interesting questions about the future of classics, which is, of course, so, I mean, a lot of listeners won't know this.
sentences.zh: 好吧，玛丽，这就引发了一些关于古典学未来的非常有趣的问题，当然，很多听众可能并不知道这一点。

sentences.en: But in America, in academic circles, I mean, really, I think specifically in America, it is intensely controversial.
sentences.zh: 但在美国的学术界——我的意思是，真的，我认为特别是在美国——这是极具争议的。

sentences.en: So, for example, there's an assistant professor at Princeton called Danel Padilla-Peralta, who has written and spoken at length about basically dismantling classics as a subject,
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，普林斯顿大学有一位名叫达尼尔·帕迪拉-佩拉尔塔的助理教授，他写过并大谈特谈基本上要彻底废除古典学这个学科，

sentences.en: because he believes that classics is a kind of bull book of white supremacy, Eurocentrism, all of these terrible things.
sentences.zh: 因为他认为古典学是白人至上主义、欧洲中心主义以及所有这些可怕事情的堡垒。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: What's your take on all that?
sentences.zh: 对此你有什么看法？

sentences.en: Well, I think I should say that, particularly in the case of Danel, he's really smart.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想我应该说，特别是在达尼尔的例子中，他非常聪明。

sentences.en: And what he writes in Roman history is extremely good.
sentences.zh: 他在罗马历史方面写的东西极其出色。

sentences.en: I think that there's a baby in bathwater problem here, and it does play out differently in the context of post-slavery America.
sentences.zh: 我认为这里存在一个把婴儿和洗澡水一起倒掉的问题，而且在经历过奴隶制的美国的背景下，情况确实会有所不同。

sentences.en: It does play out differently.
sentences.zh: 情况确实会有所不同。

sentences.en: But I think that anybody who studies classics and tries to deny that it has been used to legitimate some of the most horrible political movements that we've got would just not be looking history in the face.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，任何研究古典学并试图否认它曾被用于为我们所经历过的一些最可怕的政治运动辩护的人，都是在回避历史。

sentences.en: I think what the most fervent of those critics of classics in the States tend to sometimes forget is that, first of all, there is another side to it.
sentences.zh: 我认为，美国那些古典学批评者中最狂热的人有时往往会忘记，首先，它还有另一面。

sentences.en: You know, as we've mentioned, you know, there's the revolutionary side, you know, go and look at revolutionary architecture.
sentences.zh: 你知道，正如我们所提到的，你知道，有革命的那一面，你去看看革命时期的建筑。

sentences.en: We think of, we think of architecture and classics as being, you know, Prince Charles liking columns, but, you know,
sentences.zh: 我们认为——我们认为建筑和古典学是——你知道的，查尔斯王子喜欢圆柱，但是，你知道，

sentences.en: look at Boulay and people like that in the French 18th and 19th century using classical forms to reconfigure the very nature of what architecture is.
sentences.zh: 看看布勒（Boullée）和法国18世纪及19世纪的其他一些人，他们如何利用古典形式来重构建筑本身的本质。

sentences.en: So, but I think also the people who use classics as a bullock for, you know, white supremacy, you name it, far right causes, usually they've got it terribly wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以，但我认为，那些把古典学用作白人至上主义、你随便说吧、极右翼事业堡垒的人，通常都大错特错了。

sentences.en: You know, they're not, they're very bad classicists.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们不是——他们是非常糟糕的古典学者。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think that possibly we could spend more of our time just patiently explaining why the Spartans, for example,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我想我们或许可以花更多时间耐心地解释，为什么斯巴达人，举个例子，

sentences.en: are not entirely admirable and represent a good model for a modern state.
sentences.zh: 并不完全令人钦佩，也不是现代国家的良好模范。

sentences.en: And I think, too, that, you know, we've talked a bit already about, you know, where the study of classics ends.
sentences.zh: 我也认为，你知道，我们之前已经讨论过古典学研究的终点在哪里。

sentences.en: And there has been a very, not just Greco-Roman centredness, it's been very centred on Italy and what is now modern Greece.
sentences.zh: 这里不仅存在以希腊罗马为中心的倾向，还非常以意大利和现在的现代希腊为中心。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think there's a lot to be done in saying, look, parts of the African continent were, you know, crucially important parts of the Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我认为有很多工作要做，那就是指出，看吧，非洲大陆的一些地区曾是罗马帝国的关键组成部分。

sentences.en: And classicists have sometimes themselves given the impression that it was a white man's subject.
sentences.zh: 而古典学者有时自己也给人一种印象，认为这是一个白人的学科。

sentences.en: Now, it isn't and hasn't been for a long time, but we ought to, I think we ought to shout a bit about that before we decide to burn it all down.
sentences.zh: 现在它不是了，而且很久以来都不是了，但在我们决定把它付之一炬之前，我认为我们应该对此大声疾呼一番。

sentences.en: And isn't there a danger as well that classics is just, it's just endangered anyway?
sentences.zh: 难道不也存在这样一种危险吗，即古典学无论如何都已经——它本来就处于危险之中？

sentences.en: I mean, classics is always a bit embattled, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，古典学一直都处境艰难，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's always, well, I think it's been embattled since about the fourth century AD, probably, you know.
sentences.zh: 它一直——好吧，我认为它大概从公元四世纪左右开始就处境艰难了，你知道的。

sentences.en: I mean, there is something about classics which, embedded in the subject, is the idea that people before us did it better.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，古典学中确实存在某种东西，这种东西植根于该学科之中，那就是认为我们之前的人做得更好。

sentences.en: Right, that's interesting.
sentences.zh: 没错，这很有意思。

sentences.en: You know, and so there's a venerable classical organisation in this country, the Classical Association, founded in the early years of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所以在我们国家有一个历史悠久的古典学组织——古典学协会，创立于20世纪初。

sentences.en: Why did they find it?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么要创立它？

sentences.en: Because they thought that classics was going down the tubes.
sentences.zh: 因为他们觉得古典学正在走下坡路。

sentences.en: They wanted to have a society that would preserve classics.
sentences.zh: 他们想要成立一个旨在保护古典学的协会。

sentences.en: Now, we look back to the early years of the 20th century as a moment when classics was, you know, you could see it everywhere.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们回首20世纪初期，认为那是古典学——你知道的，随处可见的一个时期。

sentences.en: Their perception was people aren't doing it as well as they used to be.
sentences.zh: 但他们的看法是，人们做得没有以前那么好了。

sentences.en: We need this, you know, people are always trying to put preservation orders on it.
sentences.zh: 我们需要这个，你知道，人们总是试图给它申请历史建筑保护令。

sentences.en: And partly, you know, partly I'm kind of pleased because I think, you know, although one way of representing classics is that it's an awfully self-confident, elitist discipline,
sentences.zh: 从某种程度上说，你知道，从某种程度上说我其实挺高兴的，因为我认为，尽管代表古典学的一种方式是认为它是一门极其自信、精英主义的学科，

sentences.en: which kind of involves not much more than quoting bits of Homer at random, you know, it's also a discipline that, as long as I've been involved and for decades earlier,
sentences.zh: 这其中差不多也就是随口引用几句荷马史诗，你知道的，但这也是一门只要我参与其中并且在此之前几十年里，

sentences.en: has been concerned about itself, you know, wondered what it was for, how it should fit into a modern curriculum, et cetera, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 一直都在关注自身的学科，你知道，它会思考自己是用来做什么的，应该如何融入现代课程等等。

sentences.en: You know, classicists are, you know, they're quite sort of heart-searching.
sentences.zh: 你知道，古典学者们，他们相当喜欢进行灵魂拷问。

sentences.en: They're not.
sentences.zh: 他们不是那样的。

sentences.en: Well, Mary, there's a question from Mark Woodhouse.
sentences.zh: 好吧，玛丽，这里有一个来自马克·伍德豪斯的问题。

sentences.en: If we stopped studying classics tomorrow, what would we lose?
sentences.zh: 如果我们明天停止研究古典学，我们会失去什么？

sentences.en: I mean, that's it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，就是这样。

sentences.en: That's it for you.
sentences.zh: 这对你来说就是全部。

sentences.en: I actually wrote an exam question almost exactly like that about 20 years ago.
sentences.zh: 大约20年前，我实际上出过一道几乎完全一样的考试题。

sentences.en: If classics goes, what else goes?
sentences.zh: 如果古典学消失了，还有什么会消失？

sentences.en: Was my exam question.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的考题。

sentences.en: I don't think many people answered it, I have to say.
sentences.zh: 我必须承认，没几个人答这道题。

sentences.en: But I think that we've already touched on that.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们刚才已经触及了这一点。

sentences.en: You know, I'm not in any way an advocate of, you know, every 11-year-old being put through compulsory Latin, you know, for whatever reason.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我绝不是那种主张让每个11岁的孩子出于某种原因都去学必修拉丁语的人。

sentences.en: You know, I am an advocate of people getting the opportunity to study Latin and not to be encouraged.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我是主张人们有机会去学习拉丁语且不应受到阻碍的人。

sentences.en: But in a sense, I think we've already hinted at what would go.
sentences.zh: 但从某种意义上说，我认为我们已经暗示了将会失去什么。

sentences.en: I mean, if you're going to read Dante, how do you read Dante if nobody in your culture, and happily culture is a kind of sharing enterprise,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你要读但丁，如果你们文化中的任何人——而且幸运的是，文化是一种共享的事业，

sentences.en: so we don't need absolutely everybody to have read Virgil.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不需要绝对每一个人都读过维吉尔。

sentences.en: But how is Dante going to make sense to us without Virgil still being on our cultural horizon?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果维吉尔不再出现在我们的文化视野中，但丁对我们来说怎么还能讲得通呢？

sentences.en: You know, you look at the Coen brothers, O Brother Where Art Thou, which is based on The Odyssey.
sentences.zh: 你看科恩兄弟的电影《奥德赛》（O Brother, Where Art Thou?），它是以《奥德赛》为基础的。

sentences.en: How, you know, is that kind of movie possible?
sentences.zh: 如果没有那种认为荷马仍然是我们世界一部分的感觉，

sentences.en: Is that without that sense that Homer is still part of our world?
sentences.zh: 那种电影怎么可能拍得出来？

sentences.en: I don't think that you, you know, as I say, classicists can sometimes come over a bit heavy and a bit strong.
sentences.zh: 我不认为你——正如我所说，古典学者有时可能会显得有点沉重和强势。

sentences.en: But my claim would be, and this is one of the reasons, of course, that I wrote the book, is that a visit to a art gallery, a major Western art gallery,
sentences.zh: 但我的主张是——这也是我写这本书的原因之一——如果你不知道画家们画的是什么，

sentences.en: is actually impoverished if you don't know what the painters are painting.
sentences.zh: 那么参观艺术馆——一个西方的大型艺术馆——实际上就会变得索然无味。

sentences.en: So to turn that slightly on its head, so if classics went, if there was no opportunity to study ancient Greece and Rome,
sentences.zh: 所以反过来想想，如果古典学消失了，如果没有机会研究古希腊和古罗马了，

sentences.en: I reckon that there would still be people who would want to do it desperately.
sentences.zh: 我想仍然会有人拼命地想要去研究它。

sentences.en: And one of the reasons for that is, I remember an editor years ago, when I was kind of debating what to write a subject.
sentences.zh: 其中的原因之一，我记得多年前我还在纠结该写什么题材时，有一位编辑说过，

sentences.en: And he said that, you know, the top three topics that sell to the general public, obviously, Second World War comes in absolutely miles ahead, then Tudors, and then the Romans.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，卖给普通大众排名前三的主题，显而易见，第二次世界大战远远领先，然后是都铎王朝，接着是罗马人。

sentences.en: Not the Greeks, not the Egyptians.
sentences.zh: 不是希腊人，也不是埃及人。

sentences.en: It was always, but the Romans in particular have that glamour.
sentences.zh: 一直以来，特别是罗马人拥有那种独特的魅力。

sentences.en: And I wonder that a lot of the hesitancy that kind of shadows maybe the study of classics is in part a fear of that glamour, that it's seen as a kind of almost,
sentences.zh: 我在想，笼罩在古典学研究之上的许多犹豫，部分原因是对这种魅力的恐惧，它被视为几乎是一种——

sentences.en: it's dangerous perhaps, it's hard to control because it is alien to us.
sentences.zh: 也许它是危险的，很难掌控，因为它对我们来说是异质的。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's why it's exciting, you know, but it's sheer alien-ness, while also the sense that it remains part of our world is what gives it.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是它令人兴奋的地方，你知道，但正是这种纯粹的异质性，以及它依然是我们世界一部分的感觉，赋予了它……

sentences.en: Which is what Gladiator gave, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: 也就是《角斗士》所给予的那种感觉，对吧？

sentences.en: It is what Gladiator gave, but I also think that there is huge popular intereSt.
sentences.zh: 这正是《角斗士》所给予的，但我同时也认为大众对此有着巨大的兴趣。

sentences.en: You know, you only have to look at what plays sell out in the West End.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你只需要看看西区有哪些话剧座无虚席就知道了。

sentences.en: And now we can go back to the theatre and, you know, the ancient Greek tragedy is still a blockbuster.
sentences.zh: 现在我们可以重返剧场，古希腊悲剧依然是大热门。

sentences.en: It's still putting bums on seats.
sentences.zh: 它依然能吸引观众买票入场。

sentences.en: But what you've got to realise, I think, is that why that popular enthusiasm can be sustained
sentences.zh: 但我觉得，你需要明白的是，这种大众热情之所以能够持续

sentences.en: is because there are people doing some hard, possibly not very glamorous, academic work on those texts which keep them on the intellectual and contemporary horizon.
sentences.zh: 是因为有一群人在对这些文本进行艰苦的、可能并不那么光鲜的学术研究，正是这些研究让它们保持在知识和当代的视野中。

sentences.en: I mean, I think people often say to me, well, we don't need people like you because everything's been translated.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们经常对我说，好吧，我们不需要像你这样的人，因为一切都已经被翻译过了。

sentences.en: And I said, well, look, if you think, go back to Gilbert Murray's translations of Greek tragedy in the early 20th century, hugely popular.
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，你看，如果你回想一下吉尔伯特·穆雷在20世纪初对希腊悲剧的翻译，极其受欢迎。

sentences.en: They sold out.
sentences.zh: 它们卖光了。

sentences.en: You look at Murray's translations of Greek tragedy now and you wouldn't have a run of more than a week if you tried to put it on.
sentences.zh: 你现在看看穆雷对希腊悲剧的翻译，如果你试图把它搬上舞台，连一个星期都演不下去。

sentences.en: Because actually what Murray was doing is what we all do, which is mediating the ancient world to our own concerns.
sentences.zh: 因为实际上穆雷所做的事和我们大家做的事一样，那就是将古代世界与我们自己的关切联系起来。

sentences.en: And, of course, making our own concerns seem different in the light of ancient concerns.
