sentences.zh: 当然，也让我们自己的关切在古代关切的照耀下显得不同。

sentences.en: But you sure can't do it with the rhyming couplets of Gilbert Murray in 2021.
sentences.zh: 但你绝对不能用吉尔伯特·穆雷在2021年的押韵对句来做到这一点。

sentences.en: And so, you know, keep on supporting the doing of academic classics as well as Gladiator.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，请继续支持古典学研究以及《角斗士》。

sentences.en: You are, as ever, the most eloquent defender of your discipline.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，你是你这个学科最雄辩的捍卫者。

sentences.en: It's been wonderful to have you on.
sentences.zh: 你能来做客真是太棒了。

sentences.en: But we have one last question, Tom.
sentences.zh: 但我们还有一个最后的问题，汤姆。

sentences.en: Dominic does.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克有。

sentences.en: It's Dominic here who is massively lowering the tone.
sentences.zh: 在这里拉低格调的正是多米尼克。

sentences.en: Our listeners know that we like to end with the really big historiographical kind of what they call the meta questions.
sentences.zh: 我们的听众都知道，我们喜欢以非常宏大的历史学问题，也就是他们所说的元问题来结尾。

sentences.en: So we've had a question, an excellent question.
sentences.zh: 所以我们收到一个问题，一个非常棒的问题。

sentences.en: Now, I know you've responded to this already, so I know your game.
sentences.zh: 现在，我知道你已经回答过这个问题了，所以我知道你的套路。

sentences.en: It's from Carlos D.
sentences.zh: 这是卡洛斯·D提的。

sentences.en: And this is the question I think that everybody wants to know the answer.
sentences.zh: 我想这也是每个人都想知道答案的问题。

sentences.en: If Alexander the Great fought Julius Caesar, who would win?
sentences.zh: 如果亚历山大大帝与尤利乌斯·恺撒对决，谁会赢？

sentences.en: It's a brilliant question, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这是一个精彩的问题，对吧？

sentences.en: All I can tell you...
sentences.zh: 我能告诉你的是……

sentences.en: With their armies, do we think, or kind of man on man?
sentences.zh: 你是说带着他们的军队，还是单挑？

sentences.en: Yeah, they've got to have armies.
sentences.zh: 对，他们必须带着军队。

sentences.en: It's not man to man.
sentences.zh: 这不是单挑。

sentences.en: One thing I can tell you, I'm not very good.
sentences.zh: 有一件事我可以告诉你，我不太擅长这个。

sentences.en: You're so much better at military history than me, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你比我擅长军事历史太多了。

sentences.en: And I'm sure that you could give a...
sentences.zh: 我确信你可以给出……

sentences.en: Don't want to hate military history.
sentences.zh: 我可不想讨厌军事历史。

sentences.en: Well, if he hates military history, God knows who loves it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果他讨厌军事历史，天知道谁会喜欢。

sentences.en: But what I would say is, do you know it's really interesting because the Greeks and Romans thought that?
sentences.zh: 但我想说的是，你知道这真的很有趣，因为希腊人和罗马人就是这么想的？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's like Plutarch's lives, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 对，就像普鲁塔克的《名人传》，对吧？

sentences.en: When Plutarch writes his lives, the great Greeks and the great Romans, and he puts them into pairs, you know, he pairs Julius Caesar with Alexander the Great.
sentences.zh: 当普鲁塔克写他的传记时，伟大的希腊人和伟大的罗马人，他把他们配对，你知道的，他把尤利乌斯·恺撒和亚历山大大帝配成一对。

sentences.en: So you've got a kind of double-headed biography.
sentences.zh: 所以你得到了一种双头传记。

sentences.en: And part of the issue is, okay, so which of them would win, guys?
sentences.zh: 部分问题是，好吧，他们俩谁会赢，伙计们？

sentences.en: You know, and even...
sentences.zh: 你知道的，甚至……

sentences.en: So you think, well, which of them is it?
sentences.zh: 所以你在想，好吧，到底是哪一个？

sentences.en: You're the professor of classics.
sentences.zh: 你是古典学教授。

sentences.en: What do you want to name?
sentences.zh: 你想说谁？

sentences.en: Everyone's hanging.
sentences.zh: 大家都悬着心呢。

sentences.en: Well, it's very hard because neither of them last very long, really.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这很难，因为他们俩其实都活不长。

sentences.en: So if you were to say Augustus, you know, is it Alexander the Great or Augustus?
sentences.zh: 所以如果你要说奥古斯都，你知道的，是亚历山大大帝还是奥古斯都？

sentences.en: It's very invasive.
sentences.zh: 这太有侵略性了。

sentences.en: Then I would go for Augustus because he was kind of unbatterable.
sentences.zh: 那我会选奥古斯都，因为他几乎是不可战胜的。

sentences.en: Well, I'm going to take the Roman part and say they were both absolutely horrific massacres of innocent human beings, but probably Julius Caesar has the edge.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我从罗马的角度来说，他们俩对无辜人类都是绝对可怕的大屠杀，但可能尤利乌斯·恺撒略胜一筹。

sentences.en: See, I don't want to...
sentences.zh: 你看，我不想……

sentences.en: It's foolish to disagree with a professor of classics, but I think Alexander would win because he had a track...
sentences.zh: 不同意古典学教授的观点是愚蠢的，但我认为亚历山大会赢，因为他有……

sentences.en: I said this to Tom beforehand.
sentences.zh: 我之前对汤姆说过这个。

sentences.en: He had a track record of fighting against bigger odds.
sentences.zh: 他有着在面临巨大劣势的情况下战斗的历史记录。

sentences.en: The big superpower of the day, Persia.
sentences.zh: 当时的超级大国，波斯。

sentences.en: Julius Caesar just fighting a load of ghouls.
sentences.zh: 尤利乌斯·恺撒只是在打一群乌合之众。

sentences.en: Mary, I agreed with you.
sentences.zh: 玛丽，我同意你的看法。

sentences.en: But obviously, this is a debate that will run and run and run.
sentences.zh: 但显然，这是一场没完没了的辩论。

sentences.en: What do you, the listener, think?
sentences.zh: 作为听众的你，怎么看？

sentences.en: Let us know.
sentences.zh: 让我们知道。

sentences.en: Alexander was a terrible drunk.
sentences.zh: 亚历山大是个出了名的酒鬼。

sentences.en: That was his Achilles heel.
sentences.zh: 那是他的阿喀琉斯之踵。

sentences.en: Well, you're just listening to the Roman propaganda here, aren't you?
sentences.zh: 好吧，你这只是在听信罗马的宣传，对吧？

sentences.en: I think this is the perfect note on which to end.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个完美的结束语。

sentences.en: Mary, thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 玛丽，非常感谢。

sentences.en: And thank you, everyone, for listening.
sentences.zh: 也谢谢大家的收听。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: And we will see you again soon.
sentences.zh: 我们很快再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Thanks very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家再见。

sentences.zh: 感谢收听《历史的余烬》。
